title: security(approvals): two more approval-path titles are read under the system context without the reader's field-level security (lookup-target payload_display titles; the RECORD_LOCKED refusal) — #23594's family, measure first
body:
Filing gate **①, the security exception (may leak data). First point: measure reachability first.** Both locations below are read from source by the contract review of PR #23614 (`6185049769`, ③) and are **not yet measured**. Function level only; ⛔ no reproduction recipe on this card. Filed by `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `os-bill` · session `session_017WLmd5in9RXu7AjyHR8fKQ`. ⛔ Not a claim; grade and lane are triage's.

**Family:** this is the closing card for the remaining locations of #23594's class. In that class, a record's title is resolved under `SYSTEM_CTX` and served on an approval path without the reading or acting caller's field-level security. #23594 (PR #23614) fixes the subject's own `record_title` on the inbox, the request detail, the decision toasts and the action-link pages. This card enumerates what that card's scope left out. One card covers the family; ⛔ no point cards.

**Reader who acts:** triage grades and routes it. The landing is `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals` (`domain:services`).

## The governing text

- `payload-redaction.ts`'s header (#10749): "Redaction is applied at SERVE time, keyed on the reading caller, so the same row answers an admin with the whole snapshot and a restricted approver with only the fields they may read."
- #7497's ruling C (`6051659422`): record access stays with object permissions, sharing and the application's row-level rules.

## Enumeration (each row is a location the fix's pin must cover, or close with a measurement)

| # | Location | Reader | What the source shows | Status |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `approval-service.ts` `enrichRows`, the `payload_display` lookup-target titles | a routed approver reading the inbox or the request detail | The lookup keys come from the reader-redacted snapshot, so a withheld lookup field lends nothing. A readable lookup field's TARGET is titled from the whole target record under `SYSTEM_CTX`, narrowed only by the target object's declared exposure (#22738), not by the reader's field-level security on the target's display field. | read, not measured |
| 2 | `lifecycle-hooks.ts` `recordTitleOf`, the `RECORD_LOCKED` refusal | a WRITER refused while an approval holds the record | The refusal names the record's title, taken from the engine's update pre-image (`ctx.previous`). Whether that pre-image is narrowed by the writer's field-level security was not measured. | read, not measured |

## What done looks like

- **Row 1:** a target title is served only when the reader may read the target's display field, with the same served-fields rule PR #23614 applies to the subject (`resolveReadableSnapshotFields` as the reader, on the target object). Pins: a restricted reader gets the target's id rather than its title, a permitted reader still gets the title, and each negative pin is ablated.
- **Row 2:** measure first. If a writer whose field-level security withholds the display field can be told its value by the refusal, the refusal names the record by id (or by what the writer may read). If it cannot, close the row with the measurement.
- ⛔ No grant to anyone. ⛔ No new gate.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included:
- `approvals payload_display lookup target title field-level security reader SYSTEM_CTX referenced record title redaction`: 7 hits. #23594 (open; the subject title, the positive control) and #22738 (closed; the targets' declared exposure, not reader FLS). #20964, #23093, #22211, #22538 and #20044 are closed and different.
- `RECORD_LOCKED refusal names record title approval lock writer field-level security recordTitleOf`: 14 hits. #23594 came back as the positive control. #21755 (closed; the attachment gate's refusals naming a parent record) is the nearest sibling, in another package. None covers either row.
